battle.name: 隋平楊玄感之戰
battle.brief: 大業九年三月，隋煬帝百萬大軍東征高句麗，畿輔空虛，天下饑荒。楊玄感於黎陽舉兵，眾至數萬，沿官道西進猛攻洛陽不下；隋將宇文述率精騎五千自涿郡南下，追至谷城破之，玄感與諸弟盡歿。卡面羅馬方陣盾雖非隋制，「盾緣相咬成面」的原理可對照隋軍步盾結陣與起義軍有盾無攻城器的窘境。

kit.name: 羅馬方陣盾
kit.history: 凸面的長方盾。羅馬的防線靠盾緣咬住盾緣，不是靠盾牌多厚。

countries: 本役交戰的兩方，一方是隋朝中央與東都留守系統。隋煬帝楊廣於大業九年正月發兵百十三萬、號二百萬，再征高句麗，主力屯於涿郡與遼東一線，畿輔及河南各州郡只餘老弱與徵發未畢之卒。洛陽方面由留守大將與禁軍宿衛居中，調兵、運糧、徵發皆由尚書省與度支經手，郡縣守令各保部曲，民間「五兵」之制（笄、弩、槊、刀、盾）仍照舊造徵。另一方是楊玄感在黎陽聚眾組成的起義軍，成分雜亂，以黎陽、河南饑民、鄉勇、散兵為主，號令出於楊玄感一人，糧秣靠沿途徵括與自備，攻城器械幾乎空白。河北的劉寶義、其子劉士龍，以及上洛、幽州、莒州、長平等處的響應者，與黎陽本部遙相聲援，使隋廷必須分兵應對。起義方並無正式建制，與隋方在編制、補給、器械上皆不成比例，卻搶在主力東征、畿輔空虛之際起事，佔了時機之利；而隋方雖兵精器備、倉廩有餘，卻遠在千里之外，救援遲滯，兩強弱之勢完全顛倒。
countriesEn: Two sides fought this campaign. On one side stood the Sui central government together with the command system left behind in the eastern capital. In the first month of the ninth year of the Daye era Emperor Yang of Sui mustered 1,130,000 men, a host proclaimed as two million, for a second invasion of Goguryeo; the main army was parked around Zhuojun and in the Liaodong area, and the heartland of the empire and the commanderies of Henan were left with nothing but old men, raw conscripts and levies whose muster was not even complete. At Luoyang the resident commander and the palace guards held the centre, with the Department of State Affairs and the revenue officials handling the dispatch of troops, the transport of grain and the levies; every commandery and county guarded its own local militia, and the old system of the Five Weapons - spear, crossbow, glaive, sabre and shield - was still made and levied as before. On the other side stood the rebel host Yang Xuangan gathered at Liyang: a mixed force of hungry men, village braves and scattered soldiers from Liyang and Henan, obeying only Yang himself, provisioned by requisition and by what its men carried, and virtually without siege equipment. Liu Baoyi and his son Liu Shilong in Hebei, together with insurgents at Shangluo, Youzhou, Juzhou and Changping, answered the rising and kept up the pressure, so that the Sui court was forced to divide its forces. The rebels had no formal establishment whatsoever and were outmatched in organisation, supply and materiel, yet they struck while the main army was away and the heartland was empty, and so they seized the one advantage the moment offered. The Sui side, with trained troops, full arsenals and stocked granaries, was on the other hand thousands of li away, and its relief came too slowly; the balance of strength was thus completely reversed.
people: 楊玄感（？—六一三）為隋文帝孫、秦王楊俊之子，父以事被誅，家屬坐流；他仕隋為官，素有才幹之名，見天下苦役久矣遂生異志，是本役的發起者與唯一統帥。其戰略取巧而大膽：直取洛陽以斷東征軍糧道，再圖天下。他遣一支往略上洛，圖取關中，自率大軍沿黃河北岸西行，中途在滑州逗留十餘日招兵，兵力由數千增至數萬。隋煬帝楊廣遠在涿郡，聞變震怒，下詔諸軍討平。右衛大將軍宇文述奉命率精騎五千南下，追及退兵，於洛陽西南谷城擊破之。洛陽守將據堅城死守，並屢次出城反擊、擊潰起義軍前隊，是全役最要緊的一著。河北劉寶義與其子劉士龍在黎陽、冀州一帶起兵響應，牽制隋軍；同年長平、幽州、莒州等地亦有起兵者，構成「眾人紛起」的格局。玄感諸子與諸弟多隨軍歿於亂軍或為隋軍所擒，家族其後遭誅連，諸史對被擒者姓名所載不一，只能得其大概。
peopleEn: Yang Xuangan (d. 613) was a grandson of Emperor Wen of Sui and the son of Prince Qin Yang Jun, who was put to death over an affair and whose family was exiled in consequence. Yang himself held office under the Sui and was credited with unusual ability, and watching the empire labour under its wars for years he turned to plans of his own. He was the originator of this campaign and its only commander in chief. His strategy was cunning and audacious: strike straight at Luoyang to cut the grain road of the army in Liaodong, and from there aim at the whole realm. He sent one detachment towards Shangluo in a bid to reach Guanzhong, while leading the main body west along the north bank of the Yellow River, and paused for more than ten days at Huazhou to gather recruits, swelling the force from a few thousand to tens of thousands. Emperor Yang, far away at Zhuojun, was thrown into a fury when he heard and issued orders for the provincial armies to suppress the rising. The Right Guard commander-in-chief Yuwen Zhu was given command of five thousand picked cavalry, marched south, caught the retreating rebels and broke them at Gucheng south-west of Luoyang. The Sui commander holding Luoyang defended the strong city obstinately, sallied out repeatedly and routed the rebel vanguard - the most decisive act of the whole campaign. Liu Baoyi and his son Liu Shilong rose in the Liyang and Jizhou regions of Hebei to support the rising and tied down Sui troops; in the same year other risings flared at Changping, Youzhou and Juzhou, creating the picture of a realm in which revolt had become general. Several of Yang's sons and brothers perished with him in the rout or were taken prisoner by the Sui troops; his family was afterwards wiped out under the law of collective guilt, and the histories differ over the names of the captives, so only the general outline can be recovered.
kits: 卡面兵器是羅馬方陣盾（Scutum），製作年代約在公元前百年：凸面的長方大盾，羅馬軍以盾緣彼此咬合，成為一面連續的防壁，遮蔽正面軀幹，再由盾縫中伸出短劍或長矛；史語所謂「羅馬的防線靠盾緣咬住盾緣，不是靠盾牌多厚」，說的正是這種結構，而非單件盾牌本身的厚薄。中原與隋代並無此制式，本卡因此是一個形制對照件，用來比照隋軍步卒的盾陣。隋文帝開皇年間頒行「五兵」之制，笄（長矛）、弩、槊、刀、盾五種為軍器標準，其中「盾」即制式防具：前排步卒執大盾（漆木為框，蒙皮革或麻布）蔽身，後列執長矛，自側翼與盾後進槊；騎兵用馬槊、鎲，弩手用臂張弩與蹶張弩，遠射以床弩、彎弓輔之。起義軍的裝備則多出民間：竹桿長矛、草編與木製小盾、鋤犁、網索、弓弩，鎧甲不足，能勉力列成盾牆，卻難成隊形。攻城方面，隋軍備有撞車、巢車、雲梯、飛石、鉤援之屬；起義軍一無所有，只能靠穴地、堆土蟻附與夜襲，故久攻洛陽不下。此外，黃河漕運是隋軍後方命脈，黎陽正是黃河下游的渡口與轉運節點，起義軍據此以斷洛陽與涿郡間的水陸補給，正是其戰略著眼之處。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card face is the Roman scutum, a great convex rectangular shield dating from around one hundred years before the present era. The Roman army locked shield rim against shield rim to build a continuous wall that covered the front of the body, thrusting short swords or long spears out through the gaps between shields. The historical saying that the Roman line held because shield rims bit into one another rather than because the shields themselves were thick describes exactly this structure rather than the weight of any single shield. Neither China nor the Sui possessed this pattern, so the card is a formal comparison piece, set against the shield formations of the Sui foot soldiers. Under Emperor Wen of Sui, during the Kaihuang era, a system of the Five Weapons was promulgated - spear, crossbow, glaive, sabre and shield - as the standard military equipment, and the shield was thus a regulation piece of protective gear: the front rank of foot carried large shields (lacquered wooden frames covered with hide or hemp cloth) to shelter the body, the ranks behind them carried long spears, thrusting their glaives from the flanks and from behind the shield wall; cavalry used horse glaives and maces, crossbowmen the arm-drawn and the spring-horn crossbows, with larger mounted bows and ordinary bows for longer range. The rebels drew their equipment from the countryside: bamboo-shafted spears, small shields of wicker and wood, hoes and ploughs, ropes and nets, bows and crossbows. Armour was scarce; they could scramble together into something like a shield wall, but they could not make a formation. For siege work the Sui had battering rams, siege towers, scaling ladders, stone-throwers and hooked grabs; the rebels had none of these and could only dig under the wall, build earthen ramps and climb, or assault by night - which is why Luoyang never fell to them. The Yellow River grain transport was the lifeline of the Sui war effort, and Liyang was a ferry and transshipment point on its lower course; by seizing it the rebels struck at the water and land supply line between Luoyang and Zhuojun, and that was the point of their strategy.
tactics: 起義軍的戰術意圖十分清晰：不在遼東與隋軍主力硬碰，而是趁百萬大軍東征、河南饑荒「人相食」之際，突襲畿輔，據黎陽黃河渡口，斷東征軍糧道，再取洛陽西都以圖天下。行軍沿黃河北岸官道由黎陽西進，經滑州、懷州方向直抵洛陽，中途停留招兵十餘日，兵力由數千膨脹到數萬。部署上的致命問題是分兵：玄感遣一支往略上洛，自率主力攻洛陽，兩路互不能援，等於每一路都削弱到不足，結果兩處皆無所得。攻城時，起義軍晝夜猛攻，然無撞車、雲梯、飛石等重器，士卒多新集、器械雜亂、配合生疏，而洛陽守軍憑城堞、弩械與出城反擊屢挫其鋒，故久攻不克。撤退本身亦失控：聞宇文述騎兵逼近，軍心已散，倉皇退兵，隊伍在途中被追騎追上，谷城一戰全線崩潰，數萬眾一夕瓦解。對照卡面的羅馬方陣盾，其縱深整齊的盾牆靠嚴格的交替動作與統一步調維持，而起義軍既無此等編制，也無可用攻城器械，這正是它能聚兵而不能攻城、能野戰而不能守城的根源。
tacticsEn: The tactical intent of the rebels was plain enough: rather than meet the main Sui army in Liaodong, they struck into the heartland while a million men were away in the east and Henan was so famine-stricken that people were eating one another. They seized Liyang on the Yellow River, cut the grain road of the expeditionary army, and moved to take the western capital at Luoyang in the hope of the whole realm. The march went west from Liyang along the north-bank highway, through Huazhou towards Luoyang, with more than ten days spent gathering recruits on the way, the force growing from a few thousand to tens of thousands. The fatal flaw in the deployment was the division of the army: Yang sent one detachment towards Shangluo while he took the main body against Luoyang, and the two could not support one another, so each was thinned to the point of impotence and both ended with nothing. At the siege the rebels attacked day and night, but they had no battering rams, scaling ladders or stone-throwers, their soldiers were newly raised, their equipment heterogeneous and their drill poor, while the Sui garrison, using the walls, the crossbows and sallies from the gates, repeatedly checked their assault; hence the city was never taken. The withdrawal itself went out of control as well: on word that Yuwen Zhu's cavalry was closing in, the army lost heart, broke up in haste, was overtaken on the road by the pursuers, and was shattered in a single afternoon at Gucheng, tens of thousands dissolving overnight. Set against the Roman scutum on the card, whose deep, orderly shield wall depended on strict relief drill and a uniform step, the rebels had neither such an organisation nor usable siege engines; that was the root of why they could gather an army but not take a city, and fight in the field but not hold one.
data: 可核的數字大致如下。《資治通鑑》記大業九年正月隋煬帝「發兵百十三萬，號二百萬」，連同運糧輜重之民力動以百萬計，是隋朝空前規模的役使；同年秋，隋軍主力因疫病退兵，東征再度無功，可見國內留防之薄。起義軍方面，初起兵時眾僅數千，兵鋒指向黎陽縣城與黃河渡口，及至滑州招兵，眾至數萬，攻洛陽時仍以數萬計。隋方追兵，宇文述率精騎五千自涿郡南下，另會各道援軍，總數當遠過五千，但確切數目諸史未詳。守城一方的洛陽禁軍與徵發府兵人數亦無確載。時間上，自起兵到谷城敗亡不足兩月，約數十日而已。距離上，黎陽至洛陽沿黃河北岸官道約五百餘里，隋代驛程急行約需十日上下；洛陽至谷城僅數十里，追騎一日可達，故退兵途中即被追上。糧食方面，河南連歲饑荒，「人相食」之記載見於史乘，州郡倉廩空虛，起義軍沿途所取有限，隋軍卻有洛陽與黃河漕運之補給，此消彼長，是戰局逆轉的實質。至於雙方確切死傷與俘虜數，史料記載殘缺，諸說並存，此處不敢臆造數字。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked are roughly as follows. The Zizhi Tongjian records that in the first month of the ninth year of Daye Emperor Yang of Sui dispatched 1130,000 men, proclaimed as two million, the labour of transporting grain and baggage pushing the real total of people involved into the hundreds of thousands - the largest mobilisation the Sui had ever attempted. In the autumn of the same year the main Sui army withdrew because of epidemic disease and the eastern campaign again came to nothing, which shows how thin the home defences were. On the rebel side, the host numbered only a few thousand at the outset, directed at the county seat of Liyang and the ferry crossings of the Yellow River; by Huazhou, after recruiting, it had grown to tens of thousands, and the force besieging Luoyang was still counted in tens of thousands. Of the Sui pursuers, Yuwen Zhu led five thousand picked cavalry south from Zhuojun and was joined by reinforcements from the circuits; the total must have been well above five thousand, though no exact figure is recorded. The strength of the Luoyang garrison and of the conscripted militia there is likewise not precisely documented. In time, the whole affair from the rising to the defeat at Gucheng lasted less than two months, roughly a few dozen days. In distance, the highway along the north bank of the Yellow River from Liyang to Luoyang runs some five hundred li or more, which the Sui courier service covered in about ten days at forced march; Gucheng lies only a few dozen li from Luoyang, a single day's ride for the pursuers, so the fleeing army was overtaken on the road. As for provisions, Henan was famine-stricken for successive years, the records speak of people eating one another, and the granaries of the commanderies were empty; what the rebels could pick up along the way was slight, while the Sui drew on the stores of Luoyang and the river transport. That was the substance of the reversal. As for exact casualty and prisoner figures on both sides, the sources are fragmentary and the accounts conflict, and no figures are invented here.
cause: 起義的直接導火線，是隋煬帝在天下已疲的情況下再舉東征。大業九年正月，隋廷以百十三萬大軍第二次征伐高句麗，役使的丁夫與轉輸之民眾遍於河南河北，耕稼失時，倉廩空虛，加之大水與飢饉，河南遂至「人相食」、父子不能相保的地步。人心盡失之際，隋廷卻仍把主力與糧運投入遼東，畿輔與東都周邊只餘老弱，給了舉事者以可乘之機。楊玄感本人出身帝室，其父秦王楊俊因事被誅，家屬流徙；他仕隋而位不重、心懷怨望，大業以來屢進言論時弊而不見用，遂陰自結納、散財結客。起兵之後，他移檄州郡，數煬帝罪狀，以清君側除凶靖難相號召，使原本只求活命的饑民成軍。他知道正面難敵東征主力，便取最險的路：先取洛陽、斷其漕運，再圖天下。而同時在長平、幽州、莒州、黎陽、冀州等地確有零星起兵響應，說明大業九年前後隋朝腹地的崩解已是普遍現象，楊玄感不過是其中走得最遠、最成規模的一支。
causeEn: The immediate spark of the rising was the fact that Emperor Yang of Sui launched another eastern expedition while the realm was already exhausted. In the first month of the ninth year of Daye the Sui court sent 1,130,000 men against Goguryeo for a second time; the labourers and the men hitched to the transport trains were spread across Henan and Hebei, the fields went untended, the granaries emptied, and floods and famine followed, until Henan saw people eating one another and fathers unable to keep their own children. At the moment when the empire had lost the hearts of its people, the court still sent its main army and its grain transport into Liaodong, leaving the heartland and the districts around the eastern capital with old men and boys only - and that was the opening the conspirators needed. Yang Xuangan himself came from the imperial clan: his father Prince Qin Yang Jun had been put to death over some matter and the family was exiled in the aftermath. Yang held office under the Sui without much standing and carried a grudge; under the Daye era he repeatedly argued about the faults of the age without being listened to, and so began quietly building connections and spending his wealth to gather followers. Once the rising was launched he circulated appeals to the commanderies and counties, set out the emperor's crimes, and called on the realm to purge the court and remove the criminals - and men who had only wanted to eat were turned into an army. He knew full well that he could not beat the expeditionary army in the open, so he took the most dangerous road: seize Luoyang first, cut the river supply, and then aim at the realm. And at the same time there really were risings at Changping, Youzhou, Juzhou, Liyang and Jizhou, which shows that the breakdown in the Sui heartland was already general by 613. Yang Xuangan was simply the one who went furthest and organised best.
impact: 這一場所謂「隋平楊玄感之戰」，表面是隋廷速平一場叛亂，實際上是隋朝崩解的第一次大規模預演。平亂之後，隋煬帝並未改弦更張，反而再啟第三次征高句麗，役使更酷，全國民力耗盡，隋祚無幾。心理層面更深：楊玄感起兵一旦成功又迅速覆亡，向天下示範了「先取西都、斷其漕運」的可行性，也示範了缺乏攻城器械與嚴密編制時舉兵的極限；隋廷對起義者家屬的誅連極酷，株連牽涉甚廣，民間「隋必亡」的斷言因此不斷擴散。往後數年，瓦崗軍李密、竇建德、杜明威、劉黑闥、劉武周等相繼據州郡稱雄，其地盤、其部眾、其戰術，都可在這場起義中找到雛形；直至隋恭帝楊侑禪位、李淵代唐，隋末亂局才告一段落。玄感的子孫亦有流亡而後仕唐者，其家系的後續，成為隋唐之際一條隱約的線。文學記憶同樣鮮明，唐人詠隋堤、隋宮者不絕，羅隱「六代豪華空處所」一類句子，幾乎都指向同一個教訓：窮兵黷武、力竭民力者，未有不自斁其國柄者。
impactEn: What is called the Sui suppression of Yang Xuangan looks on the surface like the court crushing a rebellion quickly, but in truth it was the first large rehearsal of the Sui collapse. Having pacified it, Emperor Yang changed nothing; he launched a third invasion of Goguryeo instead, with harsher levies, and the strength of the people was exhausted, leaving the dynasty nothing. The psychological effect went deeper. Yang Xuangan's rising had shown both that seizing the western capital and cutting the river supply was feasible, and that an uprising without siege engines and without tight organisation had a narrow limit. The Sui court answered with savage collective punishment of the rebels' families, and the reach of the reprisals was wide, so the conviction that the Sui must fall spread through the countryside. In the years that followed, Li Mi of the Wagang host, Dou Jiande, Du Mingwei, Liu Heitao and Liu Wuzhou each occupied commanderies and proclaimed themselves, and their territories, their followers and their methods can all be traced back to this rising in embryo. Only when Emperor Gong of Sui, Yang You, yielded the throne and Li Yuan founded the Tang did the disorder of the late Sui finally close. Some of Yang's descendants survived the collapse and later served the Tang, and the thread of that family becomes one of the faint lines running from Sui into Tang. The literary memory is just as strong: Tang writers never stopped chanting the Sui embankment and the Sui palaces, and lines such as Luo Yin's on the six dynasties of splendour left empty point at one and the same lesson - a state that exhausts itself in war and drains its people never keeps its authority to the end.
result: 結局是隋方全勝而起義方全滅。大業九年，楊玄感部在洛陽城下久攻不克，聞右衛大將軍宇文述率精騎五千追至，遂棄城而走；退至洛陽西南谷城一帶，與追騎接戰，陣形被騎兵衝散，軍潰，楊玄感與諸弟、諸將多死於亂軍或為隋軍所擒，家族遭誅連，部眾或死或散，或被隋軍收編，或淪為盜匪，河北一帶的響應者亦相繼被平定。洛陽與黃河沿線重歸隋廷控制，東征後方因此暫時恢復秩序。從純軍事角度說，這是一次教科書式的失敗：分兵、缺乏攻城器械、士卒未經訓練而又在不利於己的平原地帶遭騎兵衝鋒，三者疊加，縱有數萬之眾亦無濟於事。但從歷史角度說，它並非真正的結局——隋廷平定了楊玄感，平不掉的是因連年役使而崩解的社會。此後六七年，烽火自河南河北蔓延至江南、關中與河套，隋朝最終在隋煬帝遇弒與李淵入關的混亂中落幕。楊玄感之亂於是成為隋末唐初亂局的第一塊骨牌，許多後來者走的，正是他未走完的那條路。
resultEn: The outcome was a complete Sui victory and the total destruction of the rising. In the ninth year of Daye, Yang Xuangan's army, having failed to take Luoyang after a long siege, heard that the Right Guard commander-in-chief Yuwen Zhu was coming up with five thousand picked cavalry, and abandoned the city. Retreating towards Gucheng, south-west of Luoyang, it met the pursuers; its formation was broken by the cavalry, the host dissolved, and Yang Xuangan, his brothers and many of his commanders were killed in the rout or taken alive by the Sui troops. His family was wiped out under the law of collective guilt, and his men were killed, scattered, taken into the Sui forces, or turned into brigands; the risings in Hebei were put down in turn. Luoyang and the Yellow River line returned to Sui control, and the rear of the eastern expedition was for a time restored to order. As pure military history it is a textbook failure: the army was split, had no siege engines, consisted of untrained men, and was then run down by cavalry on open ground; the three faults compounded, and tens of thousands could not save it. As history it is not an ending at all. The Sui court destroyed Yang Xuangan, but what it could not destroy was the society that years of forced service had hollowed out. Over the following six or seven years the fire spread from Henan and Hebei to Jiangnan, Guanzhong and the Hetao, and the Sui finally ended amid the killing of Emperor Yang and Li Yuan's entry into the passes. The rising of Yang Xuangan was thus the first domino of the late Sui and early Tang disorder, and many who came after walked the road he had not finished.
